title.en: Telling a story: had been walking

rule.sl:
**had been** + -ing pove, kaj se je dogajalo do nekega trenutka v preteklosti: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** (Hodil{m:|f:a} sem že več ur, ko sem {m:zagledal|f:zagledala} gostilno.) Kratko **'d been**, zanikano **hadn't been**, vprašanje **Had you been waiting long?** Slovenščina reče preteklik in *že*.

Pove tudi, zakaj je bilo nekaj tako, ko se je to še videlo: **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.**

Kako dolgo ali koliko: **She had been baking all morning.** **She had baked forty scones.** Pri know, own, be in podobnih ni -ing: **I had known him for years.**

V pripovedi so štirje pretekli časi:
- kaj se je zgodilo potem: **The door opened.**
- kaj se je ravno dogajalo: **It was raining.**
- kaj je bilo pred tem: **He had lost his way.**
- kaj se je dogajalo pred tem: **He had been walking for hours.**

V govoru ljudje rečejo tudi **was sat**, **was stood** (*I was sat by the fire*) in zgodbo povedo v sedanjiku (*So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me*). Pisno velja **was sitting**, **was standing**.
rule.de:
**had been** + -ing sagt, was bis zu einem Moment in der Vergangenheit schon im Gang war: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** (Ich war schon seit Stunden unterwegs, als ich das Gasthaus sah.) Kurz **'d been**, verneint **hadn't been**, die Frage **Had you been waiting long?** Deutsch sagt Vergangenheit und *seit*.

Es sagt auch, warum etwas so war, wenn man es noch sah: **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.**

Wie lange oder wie viele: **She had been baking all morning.** **She had baked forty scones.** Bei know, own, be und ähnlichen kein -ing: **I had known him for years.**

Eine Geschichte hat vier Vergangenheiten:
- was dann geschah: **The door opened.**
- was gerade los war: **It was raining.**
- was vorher war: **He had lost his way.**
- was vorher schon im Gang war: **He had been walking for hours.**

Gesprochen sagt man auch **was sat**, **was stood** (*I was sat by the fire*) und erzählt im Präsens (*So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me*). Geschrieben gilt **was sitting**, **was standing**.
rule.it:
**had been** + -ing dice che cosa era in corso fino a un momento del passato: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** (Camminavo da ore quando ho visto la locanda.) Breve **'d been**, al negativo **hadn't been**, la domanda **Had you been waiting long?** L'italiano dice l'imperfetto e *da*.

Dice anche perché una cosa era così, quando si vedeva ancora: **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.**

Quanto tempo o quanti: **She had been baking all morning.** **She had baked forty scones.** Con know, own, be e simili niente -ing: **I had known him for years.**

Un racconto ha quattro passati:
- che cosa è successo dopo: **The door opened.**
- che cosa stava succedendo: **It was raining.**
- che cosa era successo prima: **He had lost his way.**
- che cosa era in corso prima: **He had been walking for hours.**

A voce si dice anche **was sat**, **was stood** (*I was sat by the fire*) e si racconta al presente (*So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me*). Per iscritto vale **was sitting**, **was standing**.
rule.en:
**had been** + -ing says what had been going on up to a moment in the past: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** Short **'d been**, with not **hadn't been**, to ask **Had you been waiting long?**

It also says why something was so, when you could still see it: **His boots were wet: he had been walking in the beck.**

How long or how many: **She had been baking all morning.** **She had baked forty scones.** With know, own, be and the like, no -ing: **I had known him for years.**

A story has four past tenses:
- what happened next: **The door opened.**
- what was going on: **It was raining.**
- what came before: **He had lost his way.**
- what had been going on before: **He had been walking for hours.**

In talk people also say **was sat**, **was stood** (*I was sat by the fire*) and tell a story in the present (*So I'm walking up the fell and this man comes up to me*). Writing wants **was sitting**, **was standing**.

rule.sl: Kaj se je dogajalo do trenutka v preteklosti: **had been** + -ing: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** V pripovedi: **The door opened.** (potem) **It was raining.** (ravno) **He had lost his way.** (pred tem) **He had been walking.** (pred tem, dolgo)
rule.de: Was bis zu einem Moment damals im Gang war: **had been** + -ing: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** In einer Geschichte: **The door opened.** (dann) **It was raining.** (gerade) **He had lost his way.** (vorher) **He had been walking.** (vorher, lange)
rule.it: Che cosa era in corso fino a un momento del passato: **had been** + -ing: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** In un racconto: **The door opened.** (dopo) **It was raining.** (in corso) **He had lost his way.** (prima) **He had been walking.** (prima, a lungo)
rule.en: What had been going on up to a moment then: **had been** + -ing: **I had been walking for hours when I saw the inn.** In a story: **The door opened.** (next) **It was raining.** (going on) **He had lost his way.** (before) **He had been walking.** (before, for a while)

tip.sl: 💡 Slovensko *{m:hodil|f:hodila} sem že več ur* je **I had been walking for hours**, ko govoriš o preteklosti.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch *ich wartete seit einer Stunde*, Englisch **I had been waiting for an hour**: nicht *was waiting since*.
tip.it: 💡 L'italiano *aspettavo da un'ora* è **I had been waiting for an hour**.
tip.en: 💡 How long up to a moment then: **had been** + -ing.
